clue.text: A platinum blonde finally failing to use her wiles?

indicators.note: the letters of 'a platinum' fail to hold their order, so they are reworked into a new arrangement
finally points to the closing letter of the word blonde

explanation.surface: A peroxide-blonde schemer finds her charms are not working on her target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges A PLATINUM together with E, the last letter of 'blonde' picked out by 'finally'. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To use feminine wiles is to work on someone deviously, steering them by charm: a synonym.

clue.text: Obliged to get engineer in to car

indicators.note: in tells us the engineer's letters go inside the word for a car

parts.note: a Ford is a make of car
CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer

explanation.surface: Someone has to bring a mechanic in to look at their car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'to get' and the second 'to' are link words. Ford is an American car maker familiar worldwide.
explanation.definitionFit: To be obliged to do something is to be made to do it, compelled: a synonym.

clue.text: Short lawn leads to pond in poet's village

indicators.note: short means the word for lawn loses its last letter

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass
a mere is a small lake or pond

explanation.surface: A path across a little lawn reaches the duck pond in a writer's home village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts GRASS to GRAS. GRASMERE is the Lake District village where William Wordsworth lived; 'leads to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth, the Romantic poet, made his home at Dove Cottage in this Lake District village.

clue.text: A disturbance, judge intervening to regulate

indicators.note: intervening means the judge's letter comes between the letters of the word for a disturbance

parts.note: a dust, as in 'kick up a dust', is a commotion or row

explanation.surface: A judge steps in to calm a commotion in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intervening' places J inside DUST, after the A; 'to' is a link. A 'dust' as a row is chiefly British informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust a mechanism is to set or tune it correctly: a synonym.

clue.text: Shabby old magistrate, a left-winger

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of old Venice or Genoa
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A scruffy elderly judge turns out to be a socialist.
explanation.walkthrough: A doge was the elected chief magistrate of the Venetian republic.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-eared book has its page corners folded down from wear, so it looks worn and tatty.

clue.text: Not get the girl

definitions.meaning: to fail to catch or obtain something

explanation.surface: A suitor fails to win the woman he is courting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link word between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to catch something is to let it slip, and a young unmarried woman bears this title.

clue.text: Nothing going to blossom in western county

indicators.note: going to means the letter for nothing is attached to the word for blossom, coming after it

parts.note: may is hawthorn blossom
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: In a western region, flowers come to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' attaches O after MAY. MAYO is a county in the west of Ireland; may is the British name for hawthorn blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo lies on Ireland's Atlantic coast in the province of Connacht.

clue.text: Circular letter of complaint

parts.note: a petition of grievance whose signatures were written in a ring so that no ringleader could be picked out; the phrase also names a letter copied to many people

explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like it means a letter sent to many, but it also describes the ring of names on the old petition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors protesting to their captain signed in a circle so no one name headed the protest.

clue.text: Harry can relieve sub not fit for duty

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A team can bring a substitute on to replace a player who is unfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' rearranges CAN RELIEVE SUB; it reads like a player's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment unfit for use is out of order and cannot be operated: a synonym.

clue.text: Top delights, distractingly offered with bread

definitions.text: Top delights, distractingly offered with bread

parts.words: Top delights, distractingly offered with bread
parts.note: shows under the big top, given with food by Roman rulers to keep the people's minds off politics

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is the big top, the circus tent; the Roman poet Juvenal's phrase 'bread and' these sums up rulers buying popularity with food and entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman emperors kept the populace quiet with free grain and spectacles in the arena.

clue.text: Find it literally hard to be restive

definitions.meaning: read word by word, the answer says 'not easy', which is what finding something hard means

explanation.surface: Someone finds it difficult to stay calm and still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' tells you to read the answer as its parts, UN + EASY; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling restless and agitated is being troubled or anxious: a synonym.

clue.text: Cross about twin daughters' mix-up

indicators.note: about means the word for a cross goes round the twin letters

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey
D is the abbreviation for daughter, so two of them are DD

explanation.surface: A parent is annoyed about a confusion over twin girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry' but is the hybrid animal; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mix-up is a confusion or mess: a synonym.

clue.text: Showed interest in being elected

definitions.meaning: yielded a profit, as an investment brings back interest
chosen as a member of parliament by the voters

explanation.surface: A candidate was keen on winning the election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in being' is a link. A British MP is said to be 'returned' for a constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment that yields interest has paid back money; an MP voted in is declared winner for a seat.

clue.text: In part of London, confusing car routes will trap new driver

indicators.note: will trap means the new driver's letter is caught inside the rearranged letters
confusing means the letters of 'car routes' are mixed up

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a new driver's car

explanation.surface: In a London district, tangled roads for cars will catch out a learner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' rearranges CAR ROUTES and 'will trap' puts L inside. L is the British learner plate. EARLS COURT is a district of west London; 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls Court is a district in the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea.

clue.text: What may sweetly be given to waitress showing perfection?

definitions.text: What may sweetly be given to waitress
definitions.meaning: a request for a dessert of baked fruit pastry that a diner gives to the person serving
a state of complete neatness and order

explanation.surface: A diner pays a waitress a sweet compliment for flawless service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetly' points to a dessert: the first part is a request for the pudding made to a waitress; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid out in perfect tidiness is said to be in this neat state, an idiom.

clue.text: Stop by briefly with letter one stuck up

parts.note: to pop in is to make a short visit
jay is the spelt-out name of the letter J

explanation.surface: A conceited person drops in for a quick visit with a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. A POPINJAY is a vain, conceited person, originally a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain, conceited show-off is someone snooty and full of themselves.

clue.text: In the open air, pupils put in shade

parts.note: out of doors is out
a class is a group of pupils

explanation.surface: A teacher takes the pupils outside to sit in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone in the shade is to surpass them easily: an idiom.

clue.text: Gauge why office post is still unopened?

definitions.meaning: a pattern or guide used for measuring or shaping

definitions.text: why office post is still unopened
definitions.meaning: the stand-in office worker has arrived behind time, so the letters lie unread

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why the office mail has still not been opened.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part reads as TEMP LATE: the temporary office worker who opens the post is late.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern or guide used to cut or check a shape works as a measuring standard.

clue.text: A look round garden plot in a measure of reflected sunlight

indicators.note: round means the word for look goes around the garden plot

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or behold
a bed is a plot of garden for flowers

explanation.surface: Someone glances round a flower bed and judges how much sunshine it reflects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal and 'in' a link. 'Lo', as in 'lo and behold', is an archaic call to look.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers rate a planet's or surface's reflectivity as the fraction of incoming light it sends back.

clue.text: Extremely tough race for flier

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters, first and last, of the word tough

parts.note: to rush is to race or hurry

explanation.surface: A bird wins a very hard race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' is a bird: a song thrush.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrush is a songbird, so it is something that flies.

clue.text: Theatre has had to include production short of originality

indicators.note: to include means the letters are contained within the words theatre has had

explanation.surface: A theatre has been forced to stage a revival lacking any fresh ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' signals the run of letters inside 'theatRE HAS Had'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehash is old material reworked and presented again, so it lacks fresh invention.

clue.text: In house, bishop and aristocrat socialise

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a nob is a toff or aristocrat

explanation.surface: In a stately home, a bishop and a lord mingle socially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link. 'Nob' is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix socially with people, often those of higher rank: a synonym.

clue.text: Have to provide name for Welshman

parts.note: to owe something is to be obliged to hand it over

explanation.surface: Someone must supply a name for a man from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. OWEN is a common Welsh man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Owen is a traditional Welsh forename, so it can stand for a man from Wales.

clue.text: Police approaching pirate in cutter

parts.note: the Bill, or Old Bill, is British slang for the police
Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: Officers close in on a pirate aboard a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' looks like a boat but is a tool; 'approaching' and 'in' are links. A BILLHOOK is a hooked blade for cutting branches.
explanation.definitionFit: A billhook is a curved chopping blade used for pruning and hedging, so it is a tool that cuts.

clue.text: Whatever happens, don't go on staring

definitions.meaning: in any case, no matter what
look at something less, read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop gazing, no matter what.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as REGARD LESS: look less.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying on in any case means acting without concern for circumstances; to look at something less is to give it less attention.

clue.text: Tender love on the rebound

indicators.note: on the rebound means the word for love bounces back, read in the reverse direction

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: A tender heart after a failed romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' as in painful, not gentle: 'on the rebound' turns EROS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender spot hurts when touched, so it is painful.
